record.context_brief: Picard group of polarized K3 moduli
record.original_question: Let M_{2n}^{K3} be the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2n. Do the Noether–Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group Pic(M_{2n}^{K3}) ⊗_Z Q?

evidence.quote: The Noether-Lefschetz loci parameterize K3 surfaces with higher rank Picard lattices.
Q7. Do the Noether-Lefschetz divisors span Pic(MK3 2n ) ⊗Z Q?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n}$ denote the moduli space of complex polarized K3 surfaces of degree $2n$, i.e. pairs $(X,L)$ where $X$ is a smooth complex K3 surface and $L\in\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ is a primitive ample line bundle with $L^2=2n$. For each pair of integers $(h,d)$ with $h>0$ such that the lattice generated by $L$ together with an additional class $\beta\in\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ satisfying $\beta^2=2h-2$ and $\beta\cdot L=d$ has rank $2$ and signature $(1,1)$, the corresponding Noether–Lefschetz locus $D_{h,d}\subset\mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n}$ is the closure of the set of polarized K3 surfaces $(X,L)$ admitting such an extra class; these loci are divisors, called the Noether–Lefschetz divisors.

Question: Do the Noether–Lefschetz divisors $D_{h,d}$ span the rational Picard group $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (the Noether–Lefschetz conjecture of Maulik–Pandharipande) was proved affirmatively by Bergeron, Li, Millson, and Moeglin in "The Noether-Lefschetz conjecture and generalizations" (Inventiones Math. 208 (2017), 501–552; arXiv:1412.3774), showing that Noether–Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group of the moduli space of quasi-polarized K3 surfaces, as a consequence of a more general theorem on special cycles in arithmetic manifolds of orthogonal type.

status_evidence.title: The Noether-Lefschetz conjecture and generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the Noether-Lefschetz conjecture on the moduli space of quasi-polarized K3 surfaces. This is deduced as a particular case of a general theorem...
status_evidence.claim: Bergeron–Li–Millson–Moeglin prove the Noether–Lefschetz conjecture, i.e. that NL divisors span the rational Picard group of the moduli of quasi-polarized K3 surfaces.

status_evidence.title: The Noether-Lefschetz conjecture and generalizations — Inventiones Math.
status_evidence.claim: Published proof of the Noether–Lefschetz conjecture for K3 moduli.
